claims.statement: CMake uses C++17 and independently gates the graphical client, headless authoritative server, and tests. The client links graphics and audio libraries; the headless server core uses the shared simulation and protocol with GLM, Lua, OpenMP, and SFML Network, without client graphics dependencies.

The agent-check harness requires VCPKG_ROOT and the vcpkg CMake toolchain. Test mode builds all_tests and voxellancer before running all_tests; Run mode builds the selected game or server executable, and benchmark selectors are available only in Run mode.

When the graphical client and tests are enabled, test CMake recursively gathers test sources into all_tests while excluding testperformance.cpp; protocol_tests is a separate target and server_tests is added when the server is enabled. The legacy test_performance target remains separate, with one random-number microbenchmark and three skipped world/simulation cases.

The documented default build requires CMake 3.21 or newer, a C++17 compiler, bootstrapped vcpkg configured through VCPKG_ROOT, and platform OpenGL/OpenMP development support. A headless server build still requires OpenMP but does not require the client graphics dependencies.

The vcpkg manifest pins registry baseline afa249f12f52ed8a3b919f195495ba8b330288d1, declares GLM, Lua, and SFML Network as base dependencies, and adds GLEW, GLFW3, and SFML Audio through its default client feature; the build guide records their resolved versions.
The project splits Maven-like responsibilities across vcpkg for native dependencies, CMake for the native target/build graph, and agent-check for the repository's build-and-run/test workflow.

The VS Code Build and Run Game and Build and Test tasks invoke agent-check in Run and Test modes, respectively, and Build and Test is the default build task. Separate client rendering, combat, large-fleet VSync, and server large-combat benchmark tasks are also provided.

The harness exposes rendering, combat, large-combat VSync, and server large-combat benchmarks. The server benchmark builds voxellancer-server and runs 1,800 ticks with 400 ships per team; the client large-combat workload measures 1,800 frames after warm-up.

The latest documented 800-ship development run measured 47.23 average client FPS; the corresponding server run measured p50/p95/p99 tick times of 1.572/8.271/10.017 ms, a 48.242 ms maximum, and two missed deadlines. These observations are not capacity guarantees.
